note: Ps 4's open decisions in the slot/decision schema of AGENT-BRIEF.md, converted from review.html (its `verses` templates and `decisions` array; address resolved to vós, as settled). prayed.json stays the flat draft 2; site.py merges this file over it and checks that option 0 of every decision reproduces prayed.json exactly. `mark` names the words of a form that carry the link when the form also holds another decision's slot.
intro: The Latinist critic and both judges found nothing to correct. The stylist, reading only for the mouth, marked eight of the ten verses as not yet native: “várias construções fazem ouvir o trabalho da tradução durante a oração.”

Almost every fix it offered buys fluency by leaving the Latin. That is the project’s first rule against its first style priority, and no pipeline can settle it. Switch the wording above to the stylist’s, pray it, switch back, and say where the line is. Your answer becomes the brief for every psalm after this one.

verses.4:2a: Quando invoquei, {exaudivit} o Deus da minha justiça: * na tribulação {dilatasti}.
verses.4:2b: Tende piedade de mim, * e {exaudi} a minha oração.
verses.4:3: Filhos dos homens, {gravi} * por que amais a vaidade, e buscais a mentira?
verses.4:4: E sabei que o Senhor {mirificavit}: * o Senhor {exaudiet} quando eu clamar a ele.
verses.4:5: Irai-vos, e não pequeis: ‡ do que dizeis nos vossos corações, * {compungimini}.
verses.4:6: {sacrificate} de justiça, † e esperai no Senhor. * Muitos dizem: Quem nos mostra {bona}?
verses.4:8: Pelo fruto do seu trigo, vinho e azeite * {multiplicati}.

decisions.title: How strange may it sound?
decisions.why: This one changes no word by itself. It tells the next psalm’s translator, and its stylist, what is not negotiable.

options.label: The Latin first. Its strangeness stays; the ear adapts, as it did to the Latin.
The ear first. Where a line shows the work of translation, fluency wins.
Verse by verse, as chosen below — and I will say in the note what the rule behind my choices is.

decisions.why: The image is width, against tribulation as a tight place. The Latin verb has no object; the Claude judge counts “espaço” a minor addition.

options.label: me pusestes ao largo
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 — idiomatic, keeps the width, no object supplied

decisions.why: 74 times in the psalter, 33 of them the imperative, and a common versicle of the Office besides. The word study (words/exaudire.md) found that exáudi stands beside inténde in five verses, and inténde wants “atender” — so it recommends “escutar”.

options.label: atender
options.note: draft 2 — says hear and grant, but collides with inténde

options.label: escutar
options.note: the study’s recommendation — a hearing verb, as exaudire is; free for all 74 places

options.label: ouvir
options.note: ruled out now that the address is vós: “ouvi” is also “I heard”

decisions.why: The Latin has no verb. The stylist’s ear wants one.

options.label: até quando tereis o coração pesado?

forms.gravi: até quando tereis o coração pesado?

decisions.why: Recurs at 15:3, 16:7 and 30:22, so it is a glossary decision. “Engrandecer” would collide with magnificáre.

options.note: draft 2 — the stylist hears it as assembled

options.label: engrandeceu o seu santo
options.note: one verb, like the Latin; collides with magnificáre

options.label: fez maravilhas pelo seu santo
options.note: says what the Hebrew says, not the Latin

decisions.why: Compungi is to be stung by conscience. Is compungir-se a word the person in the pew owns?

options.label: nos vossos leitos compungi-vos
options.note: draft 2 — keeps the sting and the Latin’s verb-last cadence

options.note: loses the sting; moves the verb off the cadence

decisions.why: The Latin repeats the root on purpose. The stylist could not say it cleanly.
Bona is plural, “good things”. The reader who saw only the Portuguese heard “os bens” as possessions.
A stamped mark, as on a coin or a seal; perfect passive. The Hebrew’s “lift up” is not what Jerome wrote.

options.label: assinalada
options.note: cognate with signum; three syllables longer

decisions.why: The stylist heard the participle-first opening as manufactured solemnity. But the Latin column beside it opens with Signátum.

options.label: A luz do vosso rosto está {signatum} sobre nós

forms.signatumLine: A luz do vosso rosto está {signatum} sobre nós, Senhor:

options.label: {Signatum} está sobre nós a luz do vosso rosto

forms.signatumLine: {Signatum} está sobre nós a luz do vosso rosto, Senhor:

options.note: the Latin’s order, for the eye crossing columns

decisions.why: The Latin’s masculine plural excludes wheat, wine and oil as the subject. The Portuguese does not, and the ear waits to learn who multiplied.

options.label: se multiplicaram
options.note: draft 2 — subject unnamed, as the Latin

decisions.why: ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό; Jerome’s own later word is simul. It also stands at 33:4, 40:7, 61:10, 73:6 and 121:3 — say in your note whether it must be one rendering everywhere.

options.label: juntamente
options.note: draft 1 — two reviewers asked: together with what?

options.label: nisso mesmo
options.note: the calque; leaves Augustine’s reading open

decisions.why: κατὰ μόνας. The adverb can lean on God, “you alone”, or on me, “apart”. The Latin leaves it open.
